A large, sustained explosion with a rapidly rising column of smoke and debris, followed by expansion and settling of the plume over several seconds.

A large, violent explosion occurs, producing a massive, rapidly expanding plume of dark gray and brown smoke and debris that rises vertically and spreads outward. The initial blast is most intense between 12.0–14.0 s, followed by the formation of a distinct mushroom-like column from 14.5–18.5 s.; The smoke column begins to dissipate and settle; residual dust and smaller particles remain airborne, with no new explosive activity observed. This phase represents the aftermath of the primary explosion.; A series of rapid, large-scale explosions occur along a line of structures in the midground, producing multiple expanding dust and smoke plumes that coalesce into a continuous cloud. The sequence shows progressive detonations from left to right, with visible fire flashes and debris ejection.
